title: The Hoopoe and the Land of Sheba
summary: The hoopoe bird brings important news about the land of Sheba to Prophet Sulaiman (Solomon) 'alaihis salam. (QS. An-Naml: 20-44)
moral: However small we are, we can be of great service. Deliver good news honestly and wisely.
pages: One day Prophet Sulaiman 'alaihis salam inspected his army of birds. He searched and asked, 'Why do I not see the hoopoe? Is it among those who are absent?'
It turned out the hoopoe had flown far away to the land of Sheba. There it saw a grand and prosperous kingdom. But its people prostrated to the sun, not to Allah.
Soon the hoopoe returned. 'I bring certain news from the land of Sheba,' it said. It reported everything it had seen honestly, without adding or leaving anything out.
Prophet Sulaiman said, 'We shall see whether you are telling the truth or lying.' He wrote a letter and handed it to the hoopoe to carry to the ruler of that land.
The hoopoe flew high and dropped the letter in the palace of Sheba. The letter began with the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, and invited them to submit to Him.
The queen, Balqis, read the letter and consulted her nobles. With wisdom and good judgement, she finally believed in Allah together with Prophet Sulaiman.
From the hoopoe we learn: even a bird so small can be of great service because it is honest and responsible. We too should deliver good things in a wise way. The end.
